Half length portrait of the Chief of Baham, sitting in front of a house, left to the entrance (?). The entrance is framed by four richly carved panels, which show human figures and heads (?), tortoises and snakes. Another man, dressed with a loincloth and a european veste, is standing at the right side of the entrance (see 1998.110.18).

Large slit-drum and two other small drums, placed beneath a canopy. The smaller drum in the foreground to the left rests on three legs and shows a carving. The slit-drum to the right shows a sitting human being, whose mouth is wide open. The figure holds a human head in its left hand, which is placed on the left knee. A man, dressed in a white shirt and wearing a cap stands behind those two drums, the third drum is standing behind him. A young man and a boy in the farer background.

Full length portrait of the Chief of Baham in front of a house made of bamboo sticks, sitting on a european-like stool. He holds a fly whisk in his right hand and wears a traditional loin cloth as well as a cap. The door behind his back is framed by four richly carved panels, which show human figures and heads (?), as well as two tortoises. A man is standing behind the chief's right shoulder, but inside the house. At the utmost right side of the photograph a pair of hands is visible, holding a small figure (pipe bowl?). See also 1998.112.49.

Numerous carvings, representing human figures. They are strung beneath a canopy of a house made of bamboo sticks, to both sides of a door. The door is framed by carved panels, which show animals (?). The carvings are decorated with painted white and dark pigments. On the left side of the house, a fence is made of several mats. The roof of the house is supported by four pillars, two on each side of the entrance (see also 1998.112.30).

Group of people standing on a clearance. Six boys are standing in the foreground, four of them dressed in short trousers and wearing necklaces. Men and women are standing in the background, in the front of a roof thatched house.
Entrance to the village of Bansoa. Three boys are standing on a clearance in the foreground, the houses of the village are in the farer background, behind a large tree.
Group of well dressed people, standing in front of a rectangular house. They hold numerous flags. Two african men are wearing european dresses and pith-helmets.

Two caryatid stools, one standing on top as the other. The one standing on the ground is the same as on 199.110.59. The caryatid stool on top of that stool shows anthropomorphic figures as caryatid figures. The rim of the upper stool is decorated with geometric patterns. The base of the upper stool is badly damaged by insect bites (?). The stools are standing in front of a house entrance (see 1998.110.59).

Group of people, some of them sitting and standing on mats, which are spread on the floor. An elderly man, wearing a white turban, is sitting on a stool in the middle, surrounded by sitting and standing male, females and children. The girls and women are wearing scarfs. Sheeps on the right side in the background, two houses behind the group.

Young child, standing on a caryatid stool. The caryatid figures represent human beings. The stool is flanked by a long rectangular and richly carved panel on each side, standing upright. The one to the left shows four human figures on top of each other, the on the bottom being a female. The figure on the top represents an European, riding on an animal. He wears a white european dress and a pith-helmet. The panel on the right side shows four human figures as well, the first from the bottom thereby placed above an animal (lizard?). On top of this first figure, showing a male, the carver placed two female figures, the right one being significantly smaller than the left one. On top of them there is again a male figure, above which an animal is shown, similar to the ridden animal on top of the left panel. The carvings and the child are placed in front of a house wall, which is made of bamboo sticks. A vertical rectangular segment of the wall is patterend by a geometric design (see also 1998.11.12).

Two European men (the one to the right being Frank Christol?), standing in front of a house, which is made of bamboo sticks. Both are wearing european suits and are holding pith-helmets in their hands. Another house in the background, with a man, standing in front of it.

European (Frank Christol?), sitting in a car (Peugeot), which is in front of a garage. The garage is made of bamboo sticks and has a thatched roof. A ladder is leaning against the right side of the house.

European (Frank Christol?), sitting in a room behind a rectangular table. The walls are made of woven raffia mats, the two doors of the room are closed. A shelf with books and a lamp is attachted to the wall on the right side (see 1998.110.90). There are also photographs attached on the right wall as well as on the right door. A stool is standing in front of the shelf. On the wall to the left, there is a portrait as well as a map and several photographs. On the utmost left side of the room there is a cupboard ith several open compartements.

Chief of Bamesing, sitting on a carytid stool in front of a house entrance. The hosue is made of bamboo sticks, the door is framed by richly decorated panels. The panel on top shows a row of human heads, the panels to the left and to the right show two human figures standing on top of each other. The chief holds a flywhisk in his right hand. He wears sandals,a shirt and loincloth as well as a cap. On his right side are three nude woman, one holding a pipe, two holding calabashes. On the left side also stands a nude woman, also holding a pipe, which is decorated with beads.

House entrance. The house is made of bamboo sticks, the roof rests on pillars, so that it builds a canopy. The door is flanked by two richly carved panels. They show each a row of human beings, standing on top of each other. On top of each panel stands an animal (leopard?).
Upper part of a caryatid stool, showing human figures as caryatid figures (see 1998.110.73). The rim of the seat is decorated with a geometric pattern.

European (Frank Christol?), sitting in a room, whose walls are made of mats. The woven mats show a geometric pattern due to different colours. A mask is hanging from the wall. The European sits on a caryatid stool, whose caryatid figures represent human figures. To his left stands a drum and in front of him is a sculpture, showing a seated male figure.

Njiki de Bangangté, sitting on a sofa, which is decorated with a woven textile (see 1998.110.7,1998.111.32, 1998.111.35 and 1998.112.38). The chief is dressed in white trousers and wears a mulit-coloured shirt, which shows a geometric pattern.

Chief of Bafoussam, sitting on a stool in front of a royal display cloth. Five mask dancers are standing behind his back, four of them wearing elephant masks, called mbap mteng. The masks are decorated with beads. The chief wears a loincloth as well as a necklace, which forms a snake.

Young man (see 1998.111.30), standing besides a richly carved part of a bed. The carvings show human beings, animals and human heads. The carving rests on some kind of bark (?) or shows the backside of the bed (?).

Three quarter portrait of the Chief of Basoa, sitting in front of a house. He wears a cloth which is decorated with geometric patterns, produced by resist-dyeing, as well as a matching cap. To his left a young boy is standing, holding a fly whisk and a pipe, both decorated with beads. The pipe is made of clay, showing the heas of an elephant. The frame of the entrance is made of carved panels, which show human beings and snakes (?) (see 1998.110.10).

Full length portrait of Nkanga, the chief of Banju. He is sitting on a traditional stool, which represents an elephant, in front of a house entrance. To his left, a slit-drum stands on the ground. He wears traditional clothing, including a hat, but european shoes. The entrance of the house, which is made of bamboo sticks, is roofed by a canopy, which is made of mats. They show a geometric pattern, due to different coloured fibres.

Full length portrait of the Chief of Bafoussam in front of a house made of bamboo sticks, sitting on a european-like stool. The door behind his back is framed by four richly carved panels, which show anthropomorphic figures and heads as well as animals. A man at the right side holds a fly whisk and a pipe (?)

Three quarter length backside portrait of a nude woman, whose arms, torso and buttocks are with scarifications. She is standing in front of a house wall, holding a pottery above her head. She wears a necklace, made of white beads.

House wall, showing a door, which is framed by four richly carved panels. The panels show human figures as well as animals. The panels to the left and to the right show each an animal on top (leopard?). In front of the door are two uncarved pillars, which are supporting the roof (see also 1998.110.23).
Young boy, playing the drum. The drum-corpus shows rows of human faces and rests on anthropomorphic figures. Besides the drum stands a caryatid-stool with anthropomorphic figures.

Young child, standing on a caryatid stool. The caryatid figures represent human beings. The stool is flanked by a long rectangular and richly carved panel on each side, standing upright. The one to the left shows four human figures on top of each other, the on the bottom being a female. The figure on the top represents an European, riding on an animal. He wears a white european dress and a pith-helmet. The panel on the right side shows four human figures as well, the first from the bottom thereby placed above an animal (lizard?). On top of this first figure, showing a male, the carver placed two female figures, the right one being significantly smaller than the left one. On top of them there is again a male figure, above which an animal is shown, similar to the ridden animal on top of the left panel. The carvings and the child are placed in front of a house wall, which is made of bamboo sticks. A vertical rectangular segment of the wall is patterend by a geometric design (see also 1998.11.12).

Group of 15 women in front of a house made of bamboo sticks. The door is made of mats, which show a geometric pattern due to different coloured fibres. Three large pillars are supporting the roof. The women are dressed in loincloth, some are decorated with beads. They are wearing necklaces, bracelets, anklets, some are also wearing earrings. The women are holding beaded calabashes in their hands, which are used as palm wine containers for the Fon's exclusive use. The calabashes show different finials as stoppers.

Half length portrait of the chief of Bangang. He wears a cap and a long dark shirt, which is decorated with embroidery on the chest. A young man is standing on his left side, holding a pipe. A roof thatched house made of bamboo sticks is in the background.

Full length portrait of the sub-chief of Bafoussam, sitting on a carved stool, which shows anthropomorphic figures. The feet are resting on a bundle of sticks. He wears a white european shirt and traditional trousers (?). In his hands he holds a pith-helmet. Two boys are standing in his back, one of them is holding the skin of a leopard to "frame" the chief. A house in the nearer, several other houses in the farer background. Two young males to the left in the farer background.

Two men and two boys in front of a house. The chief of Batufam is sitting and covered with a cotton cloth, which only reveals his face. A young boy, also dressed in the same manner, is standing at his left side. Both a flanked by two men, the one to the right wearing only a loincloth, the one to the left is wearing a white shirt and a cap.

Chief of Basoa, flanked by by two of (his?) women on each side. The man is dressed in a kneelong shirt, showing a white-dark geometric design, on top of a dark cloth. He wears a cap and european shoes. The women are naked. The women at the right side are older than the two women at the left side. The first one to the right side is wearing necklaces and bracelets. She also holds a bundle of leaves in her hand. The other women also wear necklaces. With the exception of the woman to the utmost left, all of them have perced ears, wearing big earrings. The group is standing in front of a square house entrance, which is framed by carved panels, showing a geometric design.

Chief of Basoa, sitting in front of a house. He is dressed in a shirt, showing a geometric design, and wears a matching hat. He also wears european shoes and suspenders. At the right side three young men, one of them holds a fly whisk and a pipe, both objects are decorated with beads. The two other men are dresses in cotton cloth, which also covers their head so that only the faces are revealed. The chief is sitting in front of an entrance, which is framed by richly carved panels, showing human figures and animals.

Chief of Bazu, sitting on a caryatid stool in front of a house entrance. The caryatid-figure represents an animal. To his left, there is a mask, showing an anthropomorphic head, which is crowned by a carving of animals (leopards?), as well as two other caryatid stools, showing animals. At chief's left side, there are two drums, one resting on three feet. There is also another man, standing behind one of those drums. The other dreams is leaning against the housewall.

Two masks dancers. The mask to the left, called mbap mteng, representing an elephant. Two caryatid stools are on the ground, one with a back showing two large human figures. The stool is shadowed by an umbrella. Both caryatid stools show animals as caryatid-figures. At the left side of the stools stands a male bowl figure, decorated with beads. A group of peoples are standing in the farer background to the left, watching the performance. In the background, a long textile, patterned by resist-dying method, is spanned as a fence (see 1998.111.15).
Young boy, playing the drum. The drum-corpus shows rows of human faces and rests on anthropomorphic figures. Besides the drum stands a caryatid-stool with anthropomorphic figures.

Chief of Banju, sitting on a caryartid stool in front of a house. In the background a group of men is standing, those to his rigth are dressed in  loincloth and wearing caps. Some of the men on the left side are dressed in trousers and long shirts, they are also wearing turbans. The two men to the utmost left are holding lances (see 1998.110.12).
Two thatched mud brick buildings situated on a Bamileke hillside settlement with terraced cultivated fields, near Bamenda.
Portrait of a Bamileke man wearing a purple and white cardigan and a red, green and yellow cap.
A conical thatched roof hut supported with wooden posts and an internal wall in a Bamileke village 5 miles south of Bafoussam.
Portrait of a Bamileke woman wearing a multicoloured headscarf and striped blouse. Her hair is twisted into a braid below her ear.
Half length portrait of a woman called Maria, who holds a sleeping child in her lap. The woman wears a dress in a european style and a scarf. A house made of bamboo sticks is in the background.

Chief, sitting in front of a house entrance. He wears a white long shirt, european shoes and a cap. He is flanked by two young men, the one to the left holds a drinking horn, the one to the right holds a pipe. The door is framed by richly carved panels. The one on top shows a row of human figures, men and women, all holding human heads in both of their hands. The panels on the left and right side of the entrance show each two rows of human figures standing on top of each other.

Full length portrait of the Chief of Baham in front of a house made of bamboo sticks, sitting on a european-like stool. He holds a fly whisk in his right hand and wears a traditional loin cloth as well as a cap. The door behind his back is framed by four richly carved panels, which show human figures and heads (?), as well as two tortoises. A man is standing behind the chief's right shoulder, but inside the house. At the utmost right side of the photograph a pair of hands is visible, holding a small figure (pipe bowl?). See also 1998.112.49.

European-style house, made of bricks. The roof is made of corrugated iron. The upper floor has five windows, which are covered by curtains made of bamboo sticks. In front of the house stands a man, dressed in white trousers, european shoes an a traditional kneelong shirt, which is patterned with a geometric design.

Group of musicians with drums and trumpets. The conductor holds a baton in his right hand and stands in front of the musicians. Spectators are on the left and on the right side. At the right side, a spectator wears a pith-helmet.

Caryatid stool, the caryatid figure representing an animal (leopard?) with a human face. The rim of the seat is decorated with a geometric design as well as animals, representing lizards (?). The stool stands in front of a house entrance.
Three houses, made of bamboo sticks and clay, surrounding a square place. The house in the centre shows a row of windows, two men are standing in front of this house.
Road, three trees on the right side, one tree in the farer background and a trunk on the left side. On man is standing on the right side, another man and a horse are in the background.

Chief of Batcham, sitting on a stool, his right arm resting on a table. He hold a glas with juice (?) in his right hand, the left hand holds a large pipe. He is dressed in traditinal clothing and wearing a cap. Behind his back three men. Two of the men are wearing traditional clothing, decorated with cowrie shells, the one in the middle is dressed in a european suit and wears a european hat. The man to the left holds a spear in his right hand, the other two men are holding rifles. On the right side of the chief two boys, one directly behind his shoulder, the other one stuck his arm beneath the chief's left arm. This boy also holds an european hat in his left hand. On the left side of the chief, in front of the table, a young girl is leaning against the leg of the chief. In front of her, a young boy is kneeling, holding the pipe bowl. Under the table, there is a caryatid stool (?), representing an animal. On top of the table there is a traditional bottle gourd, decorated with beads, as well as a white european coffee pot. A  traditional textile is used as tablecloth. The group is positioned in a courtyard (?).

Two roof thatched houses and a third one, whose roof is just being made, in the farer background. In the foreground a group of eight men, three sitting on the ground, five standing, thereby two on the right side.
Two roof thatched houses. An European (Christol?) stands in front of the right house, holding a pith-helmet in his right hand.

European (Frank Christol?), sitting in a room behind a rectangular table. His right arm rests on the table, his head rests in the hand and he is smiling directly into the camera. A vase with flowers is on the table.  The walls are made of woven raffia mats. On the wall behind the man is a shelf and a cupboard, filled with books. A canvas chair is in the foreground. A calendar with the date 22 is attached on the wall to his left.
Beaded calabash, used as palm wine container for the Fon's exclusive use. The beads are of different colours and show a rhombic design. The calabash has a stopper, it stands on a small table.

Mask, made of textile, which is entirely decorated with cowrie shells. The mask, called mbap mteng, represents an elephant. A long rectangular piece of the textile is hanging downwards on the back and front when the mask is worn.
Mask dance performance with elephant masks, called mbap mteng. Behind the three masks are in the centre is another mask dancer, wearing a big hat-like headdress.

Man, sitting on a caryatid stool. The caryatid figure represents an animal. The man is dressed in a loincloth and wears an european coat as well as a hat. Behind his right shoulder stands a young man, holding a pipe in his hand.
